title: A Giant Vanished Cliff May Explain the Grand Canyon's Missing Billion Years
summary:
Imagine a cliff so huge it would take you forever to climb—about a kilometer high, like stacking ten football fields on top of each other! Scientists now think a giant cliff like that existed about 800 million years ago, right where parts of the United States are today. And guess what? It might explain a big mystery about the Grand Canyon.

The Grand Canyon is like a history book made of rock, with layers going back two billion years. But more than half of those layers are missing—like someone ripped out pages from the book. Scientists call this missing chunk the Great Unconformity. For a long time, nobody knew why so much rock disappeared.

Now, researchers from the University of Southampton in the UK think they have an answer. They say when an ancient supercontinent called Rodinia broke apart, it created a huge cliff system—a "great escarpment." This cliff stretched for thousands of kilometers across what is now Arizona, Utah, Idaho, and other states. Over millions of years, rain, wind, and rivers slowly wore the cliff down, carrying away as much as eight kilometers of rock in some places. That's like scraping off a mountain range!

As the cliff eroded, it uncovered the very old rocks at the bottom of the Grand Canyon. These rocks are called basement rocks because they are the foundation. The scientists figured this out by studying how the land changed over time and comparing it to similar cliffs in South Africa and Brazil today.

This discovery is cool because it helps us understand how the Earth's surface changes over billions of years. It also shows that the Grand Canyon's story started way before the Colorado River began carving it. Next, scientists want to learn more about how this ancient cliff affected rivers and seas long ago.
why_it_matters: This matters because it shows how Earth's surface can change in enormous ways over billions of years, shaping places like the Grand Canyon you might visit.

background_read: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is one of the biggest canyons on Earth, carved mostly by the Colorado River.
Rocks are stacked in layers like pages; scientists read those layers to understand Earth's deep history.
Rodinia was an ancient supercontinent that existed hundreds of millions of years before the dinosaurs.
Article_Structure: WHO: Researchers from the University of Southampton in the UK
WHAT: They found evidence that a giant cliff, called a great escarpment, formed when the supercontinent Rodinia broke apart and then eroded away, explaining the Great Unconformity.
WHERE: The ancient cliff stretched thousands of kilometers across what is now Arizona, Utah, Idaho, and other states.
WHY: This helps explain why more than half of the Grand Canyon's rock layers are missing and how very old basement rocks were uncovered.

perspectives.description: They think the giant cliff theory is a strong answer because it matches similar cliffs in South Africa and Brazil.
They point out that the cliff is gone now, so researchers need more evidence to confirm exactly how much rock eroded.
They see the Grand Canyon as a giant rock history book and enjoy learning how its hidden pages disappeared.
